page: Microsoft Azure FX96ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive compute instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with a maximum clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Paired with the processor is an extensive 1832.0 GB memory footprint, delivering approximately 19.08 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational speed and memory subsystem throughput. The instance achieves uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 448.55 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 189.21 GB/sec. Compute testing reflects top-tier performance across Geekbench compilation, PassMark CPU tests, and multi-threaded decompression. Advanced Matrix Extensions also facilitate strong CPU-based inference throughput, reaching 305.63 prompt tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote attached block storage for data persistence. This architectural separation trades ultra-low-latency local scratch space for decoupled, scalable remote storage management. Cost efficiency is driven by the extreme density of memory paired with high clock-speed dedicated cores, minimizing the total node footprint for scale-up deployments.

The Azure FX96ms_v2 is engineered for demanding memory-bound and compute-intensive enterprise workloads. Key target applications include large in-memory databases such as Redis or SAP HANA, high-frequency transactional data processing, EDA simulation, large software compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
